clue.text: A prospect of low regard

parts.note: a view seen from ground level, by a creature looking up from the soil; 'low regard' also suggests contempt

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a view from the lowest possible vantage point, looking up at things.

clue.text: Lacking what is not inside?

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking is the modern sense of the preposition; the old sense means outside, the place that is not within.

clue.text: Another get-together in Rouen

indicators.note: another version of the letters, a fresh arrangement, signals the anagram

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A further gathering held in the French city of Rouen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' signals a new arrangement of IN and ROUEN; the surface also nods to the French word for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people who have met before is a get-together of old friends or family.

clue.text: The old coach gets even in a Herts town

indicators.note: the word even sits within the coach word

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, was the old horse-drawn coach
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stagecoach settles a score on arriving in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is Hertfordshire, a county just north of London; the town is a post-war new town there.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a new town in Hertfordshire, England.

clue.text: Sing at the top of the scale

definitions.text: Sing at the top of the scale

parts.words: Sing at the top of the scale
parts.note: singing that leaps into falsetto, as Alpine herdsmen do among the peaks, the scale being both musical and mountainous

explanation.definitionFit: This style of singing alternates rapidly between chest voice and a high falsetto register.

clue.text: Sort of sodium salt made by six firms in the Home Counties

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the firms word sits within the south-east abbreviation

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, where the counties around London lie
COS is short for companies, plural of Co

explanation.surface: A chemical compound produced by six businesses near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, abbreviated here by SE for South East.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a solution of sodium cellulose xanthate, used to make rayon, so a sort of sodium salt.

clue.text: Summary of a note sanctimonious book

parts.note: E is a musical note
PI, short for pious, means sanctimonious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A digest of a preachy, self-righteous volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary or abstract condenses a whole work into a brief form.

clue.text: Blast? But in moderation yachtsmen like it?

definitions.text: Blast? But in moderation yachtsmen like it?

parts.words: Blast? But in moderation yachtsmen like it?
parts.note: a blast of wind is unwelcome, yet sailors want a moderate breeze to fill their sails

explanation.definitionFit: Breezy, gusty conditions outdoors are what a sailing boat needs to move.

clue.text: Act as a trespasser

parts.note: to go where one is not wanted or permitted

explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to enter uninvited, to encroach on another's space.

clue.text: Having the spirit to make a career

explanation.definitionFit: Spirited and stylish describes a dashing person; to career is to rush along, as in dashing about.

clue.text: Thousand-dollar handshake?

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand dollars, and a handshake is a farewell, so a lavish farewell

explanation.definitionFit: A lavish farewell party or ceremony for someone departing.

clue.text: Elementary discovery of team in the tube

indicators.note: the team letters sit within the tube word

parts.note: a diode is a kind of electronic valve or tube
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A team of scientists turns up something basic inside a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound with two oxygen atoms is a discovery of chemistry, the science of the elements.

clue.text: She had an overture from Beethoven

definitions.text: She had an overture from Beethoven

parts.words: She had an overture from Beethoven
parts.note: Beethoven wrote several overtures named after the heroine of his opera Fidelio

explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Fidelio gives her name to Beethoven's overtures, so she 'had' an overture.

clue.text: Early councillor getting little thanks in victory

indicators.note: the thanks word sits within the victory word

parts.note: a win is a victory
TA is a short, informal word for thanks

explanation.surface: A council member of long ago receives scant gratitude after a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon king's council was a body of wise men, early advisers.

clue.text: Hang on back her in Under stand?

indicators.note: the turned word sits within the hang-on word

parts.note: to append is to hang one thing on another

indicators.note: back turns the word her round so it reads from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to hang something on with her at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is printed split as 'Under stand', which reads together as one verb meaning to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it.

clue.text: Pose that's adapted when the going is fast

indicators.note: adapted means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stance that suits moving at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means with all speed, as fast as the post riders went.

clue.text: Takes a pretty head for such insight

parts.note: cute means pretty
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: An attractive mind is needed for such sharp understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness of perception, keen discernment, is insight.

clue.text: One from France left the Yemen port empty

parts.note: un is French for one
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A Frenchman departs from a Middle Eastern port carrying no cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Unloaded, carrying no freight, means empty.

clue.text: Girl's name he spelt wrongly

indicators.note: spelt wrongly means the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish form of Elizabeth used as a female first name.

clue.text: I step out for the ski-run

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skier steps out onto the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared snow track for skiing is a run.

clue.text: Vain display that is recalled to one buried in the past

parts.note: pomp is showy, vain display

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Showy ostentation recalled as something long buried in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' is the reversal signal, working on the abbreviation for 'that is'; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town was buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Heraldic cross is later in design

indicators.note: put into a new design, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coat-of-arms cross is added later in the design.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-shaped diagonal cross in heraldry, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Supports in an enduring way

explanation.definitionFit: Supports means bears up, props; it also means endures or lasts well under strain.

clue.text: Number in the ring do some footwork

indicators.note: the number letter sits within the ring word

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring dances about on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure but is the Roman numeral D; 'ring' is a ring of bells, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To work a lever with the foot, as on a bicycle, is footwork.

clue.text: Unpretentious old copper lowered in status

parts.note: humble means modest, unpretentious
D was the abbreviation for an old penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A modest, aged policeman is demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the old British penny, abbreviated d before decimal coinage in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought low, demoted, made to feel small.

clue.text: Stalin was on top or was he?

definitions.text: Stalin was on top or was he?

parts.words: Stalin was on top or was he?
parts.note: Stalin was a Red at the top of the Soviet state; was he also ginger-haired?

explanation.definitionFit: Someone with ginger hair; a communist leader is a red head of state.

clue.text: Lawman embracing a Berber girl

indicators.note: embracing here joins the girl to the Berber, the two side by side

parts.note: she stands for a girl or woman
a Riff is a Berber of the Rif mountains of Morocco

explanation.surface: A law officer hugs a North African woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' looks like a container signal, but here it only joins the girl and the Berber, which sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A county law-enforcement officer in the American West.

clue.text: Where shelter was available for Confederates in the Civil War

definitions.text: Where shelter was available for Confederates in the Civil War

parts.words: Where shelter was available for Confederates in the Civil War
parts.note: the side away from the wind gives shelter, and Confederate soldiers fought on General Robert E. Lee's side

explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side, away from the wind; also the side commanded by General Lee.
